items.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023
items.q: Clifford Brown to me I think is the most impeccable, perfect soloist. Sound, everything.

ctx.x: I’d write them in the key that I found them, I think, at the time. I’d be interesting if I ever could find that book, wherever it would be. I’d kind of write them in the key that I found them in and then I’d try to work them in to different things. But the thing that’s fascinating about that is that you’re developing your language, you’re developing your vocabulary, but then as you start to understand harmony it starts to expand because you

see that something that you could play on a major seven chord you can also play on a minor seven chord and you can also play on a sus chord. So then it was like all these other applications outside of the thing. It was like this is the thing but now I found — as I understood harmony more I could apply it to more things. And then also the other thing that also would just spin me out — for instance, Clifford Brown to me I think is the most impeccable, perfect soloist. Sound, everything. And he could just play a…
It seems like I’ve seen articles from guitar players and they talk about shapes. Now that can be a hand shape but it also can be what you’re describing as a melodic shape. So which drives which?
